title: Tor amplitude and K-flat resolutions
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $T$ a scheme, and $\Lambda_T$ its constant sheaf of rings [def-kun-constant-sheaf] on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $E\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and $a\in\mathbf Z$. Then $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a,\infty)$ [def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if $E$ is represented by a K-flat complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ [def-kun-derived-tensor] of flat $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] with $\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i<a$. Moreover, the representing complex may be chosen so that any termwise module pullback is again K-flat with flat terms: explicitly, for every morphism of ringed sites (or ringed topoi) $u:(\mathcal C',\mathcal O')\to(T_{\Et},\Lambda_T)$, $u^*\mathcal E^\bullet=u^{-1}\mathcal E^\bullet\otimes_{u^{-1}\Lambda_T}\mathcal O'$ is K-flat over $\mathcal O'$ with flat terms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback].

proof.text: Suppose $E$ is represented by the asserted K-flat complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$. For every module sheaf $\mathcal M$ in degree zero, [def-kun-derived-tensor] computes $E\otimes^L_\Lambda\mathcal M$ by $\mathcal E^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M$. Its degree $i$ term is $\mathcal E^i\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M=0$ for $i<a$, so its cohomology vanishes there. This is exactly the lower tor-amplitude condition of [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

Work with small site presentations in the fixed larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention], so the small-site tensor and colimit results below apply. Assume the lower tor-amplitude condition. Choose a representing complex $G^\bullet$ for $E$, and apply [lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ with $\mathcal K^\bullet$ K-flat and termwise flat. For every module sheaf $\mathcal M$ in degree zero, [def-kun-derived-tensor] identifies $H^n(\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M)$ with $H^n(E\otimes^L_\Lambda\mathcal M)$; it is zero for $n<a$ by [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. In particular, testing with the tensor unit $\Lambda_T$ gives $H^n(\mathcal K^\bullet)=0$ for $n<a$.

proof.text: All hypotheses of [lem-kun-tor-cokernel-flat] now hold for $\mathcal K^\bullet$: its terms are flat and the required tensor cohomology vanishes for every module sheaf in every degree below $a$. Consequently $\mathcal N=\operatorname{coker}(\mathcal K^{a-1}\to\mathcal K^a)$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 0F1M, cokernel construction using the argument of lemma-last-one-flat

proof.text: Form $\mathcal E^\bullet=\tau_{\ge a}\mathcal K^\bullet$ using [def-kun-truncations]: its terms are zero below $a$, $\mathcal N$ in degree $a$, and $\mathcal K^i$ above $a$; the differential from $\mathcal N$ is induced by $d^a$. All terms are flat by the preceding steps. The canonical map is the quotient $q:\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal E^\bullet$. In degree $a$, the induced differential has kernel $\ker(d^a)/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})$ and there are no incoming boundaries, so $H^a(q)$ is the canonical isomorphism onto this quotient. In degree $a+1$ its incoming image is still $\operatorname{im}(d^a)$, and all higher differentials are unchanged; hence $H^i(q)$ is an isomorphism for every $i\ge a$. Below $a$, the source cohomology vanishes by step 2 and the target terms are zero. Thus $q$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $\mathcal E^\bullet$ represents $E$.

Put $\mathcal I=\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})$. The sequence $0\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal K^a\to\mathcal N\to0$ is short exact. Both $\mathcal K^a$ and $\mathcal N$ are flat, so the last assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses] makes $\mathcal I$ flat. The kernel complex $\mathcal L^\bullet=\ker(q)$ has terms $\mathcal K^i$ for $i<a$, $\mathcal I$ at $a$, and zero above $a$, with the induced differential. It is bounded above with flat terms, hence K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1). We have a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal L^\bullet\to\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal E^\bullet\to0$.

We verify K-flatness of $\mathcal E^\bullet$ directly; a degreewise short exact sequence need not be a cone triangle in the homotopy category. Let $A^\bullet$ be any acyclic complex. Since each $\mathcal E^p$ is flat, [lem-weil-pbc-site-flat-quotient-tensor-ses] applied in degree $p$ with the sheaf $A^q$ gives $0\to\mathcal L^p\otimes A^q\to\mathcal K^p\otimes A^q\to\mathcal E^p\otimes A^q\to0$. Taking the direct sum over $p+q=n$ preserves exactness: finite direct sums of these sequences are exact by the biproduct identities, and their filtered colimit over finite subsets of the small set $\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$ is exact by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. For either chain map $f$, its tensor map in bidegree $(p,q)$ is $f^p\otimes1$; the identities $d f^p=f^{p+1}d$ and $(-1)^p(f^p\otimes d_A)=(f^p\otimes1)(-1)^p(1\otimes d_A)$ show that these maps commute with the total differentials. Thus we obtain a degreewise short exact sequence of total tensor complexes. The first two complexes are acyclic by K-flatness of $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal K$ and [def-kun-derived-tensor]. The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] has the exact segment $H^n(\mathcal K\otimes A)\to H^n(\mathcal E\otimes A)\to H^{n+1}(\mathcal L\otimes A)$. Both outside terms are zero, so $H^n(\mathcal E\otimes A)=0$ for all $n$. The definition of K-flatness proves the claim.

proof.text: For any morphism of ringed sites or ringed topoi $u:(\mathcal C',\mathcal O')\to(T_{\Et},\Lambda_T)$, the complex just constructed is K-flat with flat terms, exactly the two hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback]. Its conclusion says that the termwise module pullback $u^*\mathcal E^\bullet$ is K-flat with flat $\mathcal O'$-module terms. This supplies the final assertion, simultaneously for every such $u$, without requiring exactness of module pullback or flatness of the map of coefficient sheaves.

lean.note: The representative is a complex over the sheafified constant commutative ring. Its canonical restriction along the constant-presheaf sheafification unit is the module-valued representative of E. No arbitrary equivalence or map is chosen. The independent-coefficient K-flat predicate and IsFlatOnSite are the recorded pullback and flatness interfaces. The existential representative precedes all ringed-topos pullback data; the same P is used in every pullback conclusion. Small etale objects have universe u+1 and morphisms u, with coefficients u+1; target site universes are independent.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $T$ a scheme,
$E\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and $a\in\mathbf Z$. Then $E$ has tor
amplitude in $[a,\infty)$ in the sense of
[def-kun-tor-amplitude] if and only if $E$ can be represented
by a K-flat complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of flat
$\Lambda_T$-module sheaves with $\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i<a$;
moreover $\mathcal E^\bullet$ may be chosen so that any pullback is
again K-flat with flat terms.

proof.text:
*The model gives the amplitude.* Suppose $E$ is represented by a
K-flat complex $\mathcal E^\bullet$ of flat sheaves with
$\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i<a$, and let $\mathcal M$ be a
$\Lambda_T$-module sheaf placed in degree $0$. Since
$\mathcal E^\bullet$ is K-flat, the derived tensor product
$E\kunotimes{\Lambda}\mathcal M$ of
[def-kun-derived-tensor] is computed by
$\mathcal E^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M$, whose terms in degrees
$<a$ vanish; hence $H^i(E\kunotimes{\Lambda}\mathcal M)=0$ for
$i<a$, so $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a,\infty)$ in the sense of
[def-kun-tor-amplitude].
*The amplitude gives the model.* Assume $E$ has tor amplitude in
$[a,\infty)$. Taking $\mathcal M=\Lambda_T$ shows $H^i(E)=0$ for
$i<a$. By [lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence] there is a K-flat
complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ with flat terms and a quasi-isomorphism
$\mathcal K^\bullet\to E$. For every $\mathcal M$ the cohomology of
$\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M$ computes
$H^*(E\kunotimes{\Lambda}\mathcal M)$, so the tor-amplitude
hypothesis gives
$H^n(\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M)=0$ for all $n<a$
and all $\mathcal M$; by [lem-kun-tor-cokernel-flat] the sheaf

$$
\mathcal N=\operatorname{coker}\bigl(\mathcal K^{a-1}\to\mathcal
K^a\bigr)
$$

is flat. Set

$$
\mathcal E^\bullet=\tau_{\ge a}\mathcal K^\bullet=
\bigl(\cdots\to0\to\mathcal N\to\mathcal K^{a+1}\to
\mathcal K^{a+2}\to\cdots\bigr),
$$

the good truncation of $\mathcal K^\bullet$ in the sense of
[def-kun-truncations], with the degree-$a$ term replaced by the flat
sheaf $\mathcal N$. Since $H^i(\mathcal K^\bullet)=H^i(E)=0$ for
$i<a$, the natural map $\mathcal E^\bullet\to\mathcal K^\bullet$ is
a quasi-isomorphism, and $\mathcal E^i=0$ for $i<a$. Its kernel

$$
\mathcal L^\bullet=\bigl(\cdots\to\mathcal K^{a-1}\to\mathcal
I\to0\to\cdots\bigr),\qquad
\mathcal I=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathcal K^{a-1}\to\mathcal
K^a\bigr),
$$

is a bounded-above complex of flat sheaves: $\mathcal I$ is flat,
being the kernel of the surjection $\mathcal K^a\twoheadrightarrow \mathcal N$ between the flat sheaves $\mathcal K^a$ and
$\mathcal N$ (the Tor sequence
$0=\operatorname{Tor}_1(\mathcal K^a,\mathcal M)\to \operatorname{Tor}_1(\mathcal N,\mathcal M)=0\to\mathcal I\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M\to\mathcal K^a\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M\to\mathcal N\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal M\to0$ is exact). Hence
$\mathcal L^\bullet$ is K-flat by [lem-kun-kflat-criteria](1),
and the short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal L^\bullet\to\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal E^\bullet\to0$ exhibits $\mathcal E^\bullet$ as the cone of a map of
K-flat complexes, so $\mathcal E^\bullet$ is K-flat by
[lem-kun-kflat-criteria](2).
*Pullback.* Pullback along a morphism of schemes is exact, carries
flat module sheaves to flat module sheaves, and commutes with tensor
products and with the truncation construction above; applied to a
K-flat complex with flat terms it again produces a K-flat complex with
flat terms (the pullback of an acyclic complex is acyclic), and applied
to the quasi-isomorphisms above it produces the corresponding
quasi-isomorphisms. Hence the model $\mathcal E^\bullet$ may be chosen
so that every pullback is again K-flat with flat terms, as asserted.
